note: Adapted from the description of the species by Sjöstedt (1900), originally in Latin and German in two parts; the nymph is not described in the original. Wing length and body length of the alate, head width of the worker and abdominal length and width of the queen are incomplete in the scanned text and are not recorded; synonymy citations, figure numbers and locality collection records are omitted.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale reddish yellow, very short and subquadrate in dorsal view with slightly rounded corners, slightly narrowed from behind forwards, the middle of the frontal margin being the highest point of the head; frons truncate in profile, the surface uneven in places, with the fontanelle at the middle; head subcircular in anterior view, slightly flattened below. Mandibles slightly more than 1 mm long, black with reddish brown bases, slightly curved inward and downward, without teeth other than a rather large tooth at the base and a small tooth above it; the two mandibles mostly strongly crossed, lying almost transversely in front of the body. Labrum one quarter as long as the mandibles, deeply forked, the two branches directed obliquely outward with rounded tips, the outer margin between the two branches forming an even arc. Antennae 14-segmented, pale brown, with distinct joints, slightly longer than the mandibles; segment 1 very large, as long as the next three segments together and much thicker than the following ones. Pronotum small, about half as wide as the head, anterior margin weakly concave at the middle. Body white. Total length 5, head including mandibles 2.7.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body rather narrow, white, transparent in alcohol, the gut filled with soil visible through the integument; head tinged with pale yellow. Labrum shining and smooth, only sparsely setose, strongly arched, broadly oval, truncate anteriorly, longitudinally divided at the middle, with a brown spot on each side; two white glands visible through the labrum behind it, with a small circular white spot above the glands. Rest of the head smooth, sparsely setose. First tooth of the mandibles much larger than the others, the second tooth and the smaller third tooth forming a bidentate tooth on both mandibles. Antennae becoming brownish toward the apex, 14-segmented, segments 3 and 4 smaller than the adjacent segments, the basal segment as long as the next three segments together. Pronotum oval, the sides curved downward and rather longly narrowed, anterior lobe not concave at the middle and as long as the posterior lobe, with a shallow broad longitudinal groove at the middle; mesonotum oval, wider; metanotum wider still. Last tarsal segment only slightly longer than the remaining segments together; hind femur and tibia long. Body surface shining, sparsely setose. Body length 3.5–4.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body dark brown above, head and pronotum darker; head small and rounded, projecting forward in a slightly triangular form, weakly concave, with a small but distinct fontanelle; frons slightly flat, a low ridge apparently present between the compound eyes, with two small punctate depressions. Labrum slightly paler than the frons, distinct but not much arched, anterior margin almost straight, pilosity as on the head; first tooth of the mandibles much larger than the others. Compound eyes large and prominent; ocelli broadly oval, separated from the compound eye by about their own diameter or slightly less. Antennae as long as the head, brown with pale rings, 15-segmented; basal segment as long as the next three segments together, segment 2 cylindrical, segment 3 smaller than segment 4, the apical segments slightly enlarged. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head width between the anterior margins of the compound eyes, semilunar, the sides slightly compressed, posterior margin truncate and weakly concave, with a shallow curved transverse groove inside the posterior margin; anterior angles slightly deflexed and broadly rounded, anterior margin short and straight, slightly upturned. Mesonotum and metanotum narrowing posteriorly, each with a pair of short, rather pointed processes. Wings dark brown and narrow, more than four times as long as wide, the venation still distinct to the apex; costa and subcosta parallel, media straight and forked apically, sometimes with three to four branches, submedia parallel to the media and giving off 11 rather straight branches downward; wing scales slightly longer than wide, truncate apically. Ventral surface of the abdomen slightly paler than the dorsal, with a pale longitudinal line of variable distinctness at the middle, in the male only the upper five sternites so demarcated, in the female the pale line continuous over all the sternites and reaching near the posterior margin of the enlarged last sternite, the end of which forms two very short rounded projections; sixth sternite largest in the female, seventh slightly darker in the male. Legs distinctly dark and short, not reaching the apex of the abdomen; last tarsal segment less than half as long as the remaining three segments together. Wing expanse 20–21, length with wings 11–12, wing width 2.2.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Queen whitish with a yellow tinge; the measurements of abdominal length and width are incomplete in the original and are not recorded. Nest nodular, attached to tree trunks, with covered mud galleries running from the nest, some directed upward and most running downward into the soil; common in the Cameroon region. Nest black and very hard, built of soil mixed with numerous small gravel particles, the cells arranged horizontally like plates and easily separated from one another, their outline roughly discernible from outside the nest. Outer wall about 1 mm thick; cells of various shapes and sizes but all rather rounded, their surface flat and smooth, about 3 mm high and 12–24 mm long; small circular openings connecting adjacent cells situated at the periphery, with no opening to the exterior. The partition between the upper and lower cells is double-layered, the two layers easily separated and each as thin as paper; each chamber consists of one to two layers of cells. Nest of variable size, about 20–50 cm long.
